title: Development of performance portable spline solver for exa-scale plasma turbulence simulation
problem: Existing libraries (Kokkos-kernels for direct solvers and Ginkgo for iterative methods) are not optimized for solving a single matrix equation with multiple right-hand sides, which is a critical bottleneck for exa-scale plasma turbulence simulations.
motivation: Efficient spline solvers are essential infrastructure for exa-scale plasma turbulence simulations, requiring performance-portable implementations across heterogeneous hardware.
method: Develops spline building kernels on top of Kokkos-kernels using batched serial implementations optimized through kernel fusion and sparse matrix storage. Targets NVIDIA A100 and AMD MI250X GPUs while maintaining reasonable performance on CPUs to achieve performance portability.
key_novelty: Application of kernel fusion and sparse matrix storage optimizations specifically for batched matrix equations with multiple right-hand sides in the Kokkos-kernels framework.
contributions: Performance portable spline solver kernels built on Kokkos-kernels for multi-GPU systems
Kernel fusion and sparse matrix storage techniques optimizing batched solvers for multiple right-hand sides
Demonstrated efficiency on NVIDIA A100 and AMD MI250X while maintaining reasonable CPU performance
Reduced development and maintenance cost for spline solvers on exa-scale supercomputing systems
limitations: Limitations not discussed; abstract focuses only on demonstrating feasibility and efficiency.
primary_theme: Performance-portable batched spline solver for exascale HPC
